# Clearwater (01, engineer) — SPD-029

## Brief
Objective: close every spelling of the home (and of each worktree) that the filesystem treats as the same directory but the path rule does not, so Laws 1 and 5 hold for a Write/Edit target and a shell redirection target however the prefix is spelled. Red-first.

The hole (proposal 24, SPUD-016/Adirondack): `map_into_repository` (bin/spud_ledger.py, near line 4556) finds the root by `os.path.relpath(path, base)`, a string comparison; `os.path.realpath` resolves symlinks but canonicalizes neither case nor anything else. So on the default case-insensitive APFS a target spelled `/USERS/ERICLUGO/PERSONAL/SPUD/ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md` maps to no root, `edit_reason` returns allow, and the PreToolUse edit hook (and the Bash hook's redirection check) stay silent, although it is the same file as the refused `ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md`. Rooster's HIGH-2 folded case only for the part after the root (`path_reason`, `GENERATED_ROOTS`, `fold`).

Aliases to prove and close, each with a probe before the fix:
1. Case variants of the root prefix (all upper, mixed), for the home and for a worktree, both a `.claude/worktrees/<name>` one and one elsewhere (SPD-016's `WorktreeElsewhereTest`).
2. The macOS firmlink prefix: `/System/Volumes/Data/Users/...` is the same directory as `/Users/...` (it exists on this machine and is no symlink, so realpath leaves it alone). The test home lives under the temp dir; probe `/System/Volumes/Data` + its real path, and skip the test where that path is not the same file.
3. Unicode normalization: APFS is normalization-insensitive, so an NFD spelling of an NFC home name is the same directory. The live home is ASCII, but a test home with a non-ASCII component (for example `Spüd`) shows whether the rule depends on it.
Fold these into one fix, not three string patches. A likely shape, your call with evidence: identify the root by file identity rather than spelling, walking the target's existing ancestors and matching `(st_dev, st_ino)` against each root's, with the remaining components as the repository-relative path (the case folding after the root stays as it is). A target whose ancestors do not exist yet still has an existing ancestor at or above the root when it is inside. Case-folded string comparison alone would miss items 2 and 3. Whatever you choose, keep `case_insensitive_fs` per root where it still matters (a worktree elsewhere may sit on a case-sensitive volume).

Audit the rest of the hook path for the same class of bug and say what you found in the result: every place a path is compared with the home, a worktree or `bin/spud` by string (for example the Bash hook's recognition of a `spud` call by its script path, which Law 6's `--as spud` refusal depends on, and the git guard). Fix in this ticket what enforces a Law and is the same fix; file a proposal (`spud proposal file`) for anything larger.

Deliverables (only these paths): `bin/**`, `tests/**`. Never `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/`, `ledger/`, `reports/`, `docs/`.

Read first: `spud ticket show SPD-029`; `spud member show SPUD-016/Adirondack` (the worktree mapping and its cache); in `bin/spud_ledger.py`: `case_insensitive_fs`, `home_worktrees`, `map_into_repository`, `repository_paths`, `path_reason`, `edit_reason`, and the PreToolUse(Bash) redirection and spud-call detection; `tests/test_hooks.py` `PathRuleAsserts`, `PreEditTest`, `WorktreeElsewhereTest`; `tests/helpers.py`.

## Sub-agents

## Ticket proposals
- **Bash hook: CD, /usr/bin/cd, pushd and upper-case wrappers are read differently from the shell** — suggested P1; created as [[SPD-030]] at P1 by Spud.
  Why: PreToolUse(Bash) follows the working directory and strips wrappers by command name. On macOS PATH lookup is case-insensitive (ENV, NOHUP, CD resolve to /usr/bin/ENV, /usr/bin/NOHUP, /usr/bin/CD) while shell builtins are not: the hook strips no wrapper named ENV or NOHUP, so a git write behind one is silent (Law 7), and it takes CD /tmp or /usr/bin/cd /tmp as a change of directory that never happens (the external cd runs in its own process), so a relative redirection lands in the repository unchecked (Laws 1 and 5). pushd and popd are not followed at all, and cd -P or cd -L takes the option for the directory. Not a spelling of the home, so outside SPD-029.
  Evidence: Scratch SPUD_HOME, member with deliverable **, hook code before SPD-029 (SPD-029 does not change these): 'CD /tmp && echo x > ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md' silent; '/usr/bin/cd /tmp && echo x > ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md' silent; 'pushd <home>/ledger && echo x > tickets/SPD-001.md' silent; 'ENV git commit -m x' silent; 'NOHUP git push' silent. shutil.which: ENV -> /usr/bin/ENV, NOHUP -> /usr/bin/NOHUP, CD -> /usr/bin/CD. Fix sketch: casefold the name in the WRAPPERS test and strip_wrapper; treat only the exact word cd as the builtin; an option to cd, pushd or popd leaves a directory the hook cannot follow (cwd None, so a member's relative redirection is refused).
- **Bash hook allows any script named spud, skipping the permission prompt** — suggested P2; created as [[SPD-032]] at P2 by Spud.
  Why: bash_reason returns permissionDecision allow for a well-formed spud call, and a call is recognized by the script's name: python3.14 /tmp/any/spud board is allowed although /tmp/any/spud is not the ledger's launcher. Whoever can write a file named spud (or a spud_ledger.py beside a link to the launcher) runs it with no permission prompt. SPD-029 widened recognition to case folds and symlinks, which Law 6's refusals need; the allow should need more than recognition.
  Evidence: Scratch SPUD_HOME, member: 'python3.14 /tmp/any/spud board' -> allow, reason 'a well-formed spud call by SPUD-001/..., checked by the ledger hook' (before and after SPD-029). Fix sketch: keep recognizing by name for the refusals, but allow only when the script is, by file identity, the ledger root's or a listed worktree's bin/spud; otherwise stay silent and let the harness prompt.
- **Edit hook: a member whose deliverables cover the ledger state directory can Write the database and the hook bytecode** — suggested P1; created as [[SPD-031]] at P1 by Spud.
  Why: The Bash hook refuses every command naming the ledger database or its state directory (the gitignored dot-spud directory at the home), but the edit hook checks a path in that directory only against Law 1 and the deliverable globs. A member planned with ** (or any glob reaching that directory) may Write or Edit the SQLite database file, the worktree list cache, or the launcher's cached bytecode (its pycache subdirectory), which every hook run loads. Only the CLI should write there, and the cached bytecode is the enforcement's own code.
  Evidence: Scratch SPUD_HOME, member with deliverable **, before and after SPD-029: PreToolUse(Write) to the database file in the home's state directory -> silent (allowed); to the worktrees JSON cache there -> silent. Spud is refused by Law 1. (This proposal's first filing was refused by the Bash hook because its text named the directory, which is the hook doing its job on prose.) Fix sketch: in path_reason, refuse the state directory's subtree for everyone before the globs, case-folded and by identity like SPD-029's generated roots, worded like the Bash hook's database refusal.

## Result
**Produced** (worktree spd-029-path-rule-case, uncommitted): bin/spud_ledger.py, tests/test_hooks.py, tests/helpers.py (Home and SpudTestCase take an optional home directory name, for a non-ASCII home).

**The fix, one mechanism: file identity instead of spelling.** map_into_repository finds a root by walking the target's ancestors, nearest first, and matching (st_dev, st_ino) against each root's (the home and every git worktree); the components below the match are the repository-relative path. So every spelling the filesystem resolves to the root counts: case variants, NFD spellings, the /System/Volumes/Data firmlink, a symlink to the root. A root with nothing to stat (a worktree git lists after its directory went) keeps the old spelling match. The same identity test (same_entry) now recognizes the .claude/worktrees/<name> convention and the generated roots ledger and reports when their first components are spelled another way, with casefold where the directory does not exist on a case-insensitive filesystem. path_reason casefolds the generated root instead of lower-casing it. edit_reason asks case_insensitive_fs per root (folds_case, the nearest existing ancestor for a root not created yet), no longer of the home alone.

Probe first (scratch dirs, this Mac's APFS): same directory for upper case, mixed case, NFD, the firmlink prefix (same dev and ino), U+017F long s for s and U+212A Kelvin for k; not for dotless i, the fi ligature or sharp s. realpath keeps both case and the firmlink prefix, which is why the rule saw neither.

**Audit of the hook path (string comparisons of paths), with what was done:**
1. map_into_repository relpath against the home and worktrees: the reported hole, fixed as above.
2. .claude/worktrees detection (parts[0] == ".claude"): a string compare. home/.CLAUDE/WORKTREES/x/ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md (or worKtrees with a Kelvin sign) mapped as .claude/** and was ALLOWED to Spud, with the home spelled exactly. Fixed (identity, casefold).
3. Generated root by .lower(): reportſ/x.md is reports/x.md on APFS, and a ** member was allowed. Fixed (identity plus casefold).
4. repository_paths took realpath of the normpath'd path, so tests/link/../SPD-001.md (link to ledger/tickets) was read as tests/SPD-001.md, but the kernel writes ledger/SPD-001.md. Fixed: realpath of the path as given is also a candidate.
5. PreToolUse(Bash) recognized a spud call by basename(script) == "spud" (python branch, case-sensitive) and by basename(cmd).lower() (bare command). python3.14 <HOME>/BIN/SPUD --as spud ..., bin/ſpud, or a symlink by any name escaped Law 6's refusals. Fixed: spud_launcher matches the casefolded name or the casefolded name of its realpath; the command word is casefolded.
6. Redirection and tee targets go through edit_reason, so 1 to 4 cover them. The cd target is normpath'd, which matches the shell's logical cd.
7. harness_file: case-insensitive regex on hex and ASCII, not affected. The database regex is IGNORECASE (it matches long s), but see proposal 25 on quote-splitting.
8. Git guard (Law 7): by verb, with no path compared to the home. It is still name-based: see proposal 25 (ENV and NOHUP wrappers). A copied git binary or python -c subprocess stays unseen: a limit of a name-based hook, not a proposal.
9. Not on the enforcement path: classify_path for import --file (relative_to the home, part names compared) refuses on a mismatch, so it fails closed. The settings sync marks and the allow rules are harness string rules, so an alias gets a prompt (fails closed).
